title: Regime Structure and Entropic Flow Ontology in Discrete Gravity Models
description: Formalizes a regime-based ontology for discrete entropic gravity on graphs, showing how Newtonian (UV), MOND-like (IR), and cosmological (Yukawa-screened) behaviors arise from dominance switching between gradient, bulk, and source sectors of a single functional. Clarifies the role of the cosmological constant Λ as a bulk entropic capacity parameter that sets both the local MOND transition scale and the global screening length, all without assuming a fundamental spacetime metric.

discrete_functional.description: Graph-defined entropic functional with gradient (nearest-neighbor), bulk (Λ-locked), and source sectors; AQUAL kinetic integrand F(x) built from interpolating function μ(x).

euler_lagrange_discrete.description: Stationary condition on the graph obtained by varying the discrete functional; exhibits competition between gradient and bulk sectors with local sources.

continuum_equation.description: Continuum limit of the discrete Euler–Lagrange equation; reduces to Poisson, deep-MOND, or Yukawa-screened equations depending on regime.

poisson_limit.description: UV/strong-field (|∇Φ| ≫ a0) Newtonian limit when μ → 1 and bulk term is negligible.

deep_mond_limit.description: IR/weak-field limit (|∇Φ| ≪ a0) producing MOND-like scaling from the nonlinear gradient sector.

yukawa_screened.description: Cosmological regime with bulk dominance; linearized equation yields Yukawa screening.

screening_length.description: Screening scale set by the Λ-proportional bulk coupling; ties large-scale gravitational behavior to the cosmological constant.

regime_ratios.description: Dimensionless ratios mapping regime dominance: UV (ξ ≫ 1, η ≪ 1), IR (ξ ≪ 1, η ≪ 1), cosmological (η ≫ 1).

interpolating_mu.description: Standard AQUAL interpolating function governing the smooth transition between Newtonian and MOND-like behavior.

key_results.main_finding: A single graph-defined entropic functional yields three exhaustive regimes—Newtonian, MOND-like, and Yukawa-screened—via dominance switching between gradient and bulk sectors, with Λ setting both a0 and the Gpc-scale screening length.

sealed_predictions.statement: The cosmological screening length obeys L_Λ = μ_Λ^{-1/2} ∝ Λ^{-1/2}, numerically of order 4.4 Gpc, producing Yukawa-like suppression of gravitational potentials on horizon scales.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Detection of unscreened gravitational potentials on multi-Gpc scales inconsistent with any Λ^{-1/2} scaling, e.g., growth/lensing measurements showing no large-scale suppression at k ≲ 1/L_Λ.

sealed_predictions.statement: In the deep-IR regime, the discrete operator implies an effective MOND scale a0,eff ≈ C^2 a0 with C ≈ 2.32, i.e., a0,eff ≈ 5.4 a0, yielding MOND-like scaling from the same functional.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: High-precision low-acceleration galaxy dynamics requiring a redshift- or system-dependent a0,eff inconsistent with a constant factor relative to a0.

sealed_predictions.statement: Transition between Newtonian (g ∝ r^{-2}) and MOND-like (g ∝ r^{-1}) behavior occurs at ξ ≃ 1 (|∇Φ| ≃ a0) with smooth μ(x)-governed crossover and no additional free functions.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Systematic absence of a universal acceleration-scale transition in isolated low-EFE systems, or requirement of extra free functions beyond μ(x) to match the slope change.

kill_criteria: KC1: Empirical evidence that the gravitational potential is not Yukawa-screened on multi-Gpc scales and that no Λ^{-1/2} scaling for the screening length is compatible with data (e.g., large-scale lensing/growth) at high significance.
KC2: Robust demonstrations that the MOND-like IR behavior does not emerge at accelerations |g| ≪ a0 in isolated galaxies, contradicting the predicted regime transition at ξ ~ 1.
KC3: Measurements indicating that a0 is independent of or significantly deviates from any Λ-linked scaling across redshift, falsifying the claimed Λ control of the local transition scale.
KC4: Necessity of introducing additional free functions beyond μ(x) and the Λ-proportional bulk coupling to jointly fit galactic and cosmological phenomena within this framework.
KC5: Detection of strong-field deviations from Poisson’s equation (μ → 1 limit) inconsistent with the UV/Newtonian regime predicted by the functional.

related_packages.role: Companion: numerical verification of Newtonian and MOND-like regimes with Λ-locked screening
Companion: cosmological growth and σ8 constraints for Λ-locked discrete entropic gravity

short_title: Regime Structure and Entropic Flow Ontology
epistemic_status: Foundational framework establishing regime-based ontology for discrete entropic gravity models
abstract: Formalises the regime structure underlying discrete entropic gravity models based on graph-defined functionals. Distinct physical behaviours (UV/Newtonian, IR/MOND-like, Cosmological/Yukawa) emerge from dominance transitions between gradient, bulk, and source sectors of a discrete entropic functional. Λ functions as a bulk capacity parameter governing large-scale screening. Provides regime-based foundation without assuming a fundamental spacetime metric.

key_equations.discrete_functional: F[Φ] = Σ κ_ij F(|Φ_i−Φ_j|/a₀) + Σ ½μ_Λ(Φ_i−Φ_V)² + Σ λ_i ρ_i Φ_i
key_equations.screening_scale: L_Λ = 1/√μ_Λ, μ_Λ ∝ Λ → L_Λ ∝ Λ⁻¹/² ~ 4.4 Gpc

ontological_commitments.entropy: Functional capacity of the discrete network, not thermodynamic entropy
ontological_commitments.energy_flow: Gradient energy redistribution on the graph
ontological_commitments.lambda: Bulk entropic capacity — anchoring strength to cosmological background Φ_V
ontological_commitments.spacetime: Emergent from graph structure, not fundamental
ontological_commitments.time: Equilibrium condition δF/δΦ_i = 0; dynamics is relaxation

open_problems: Derivation of temporal dynamics from functional
falsification_criteria: Three regimes fail to be exhaustive for any field configuration
Transitions require additional free functions beyond μ(x) and μ_Λ ∝ Λ
Λ cannot simultaneously set a₀ and L_Λ consistently
Numerical verification in companion papers becomes inconsistent
